key_idea: A circle can hide under another one. Follow each round edge all the way around.
steps: There are 5 circles: blue, pink, green, yellow and purple.
The frog sits on the pink circle, so it is inside the pink circle.
The blue circle goes on under the pink one. Follow its round edge: it passes to the right of the frog, so the frog is inside the blue circle too.
The green, yellow and purple circles are far from the frog. So the frog is inside 2 circles.

choice_feedback.A: The blue circle goes on under the pink one, and the frog is inside it too.
choice_feedback.C: The green, yellow and purple circles do not reach the frog.
choice_feedback.D: The green, yellow and purple circles do not reach the frog.
choice_feedback.E: Only 2 of the 5 circles reach the frog.

review.note: The frog is inside 2 circles by geometry (blue and pink), but the pink circle's solid fill hides the blue circle's edge, so the frog looks like it is only on pink and a child may answer 1. Consider making the circles see-through or drawing every outline on top.
